evidence: `viralscan -o o4 ... --ncbi-api-key SECRETKEY123 --ncbi-email me@lumc.nl` -> grep o4/run_manifest.json: `"ncbi_api_key": "SECRETKEY123"` and `"ncbi_email": "me@lumc.nl"` stored in options (vars(args) minus a small exclude set) and hashed into run_fingerprint. evidence: Run launched from dir w with relative paths (-s1 a_R1.fastq -i idx.idx ...), manifest options keep the relative strings. `cd /tmp && viralscan validate-run $S/w/o4` -> issues missing_input for idx.idx, a_R1.fastq, a_R2.fastq, t2g.txt; from the original cwd they resolve. build_run_manifest hashes Path(v).expanduser().resolve() but validate_run uses Path(values[i]) with no expanduser/resolve and cwd-relative. Also could report a false input_fingerprint_mismatch if cwd holds a different same-named file.
proposed_fix: Store resolved absolute paths in a separate manifest field (e.g. input_paths) and verify those; expanduser+resolve as at build time.

evidence: repro_C/build_ref_no_overwrite_probe.py: kb ref cmd = `kb ref -i index.idx -g t2g.txt -f1 cdna.fa combined.fa combined.gtf`; '--overwrite' in cmd: False. kb_python 0.30.2 ref.py:642-674 skips cDNA/t2g generation and kallisto index when cdna.fa/index.idx exist (`Skipping kallisto index because ... already exists. Use the --overwrite flag`). So build-ref into a non-empty --output (changed accession list, --no-mask, new Ensembl release) rewrites combined.fa/gtf and reference_manifest.json (content_files hashes of NEW files, index sha256 of OLD index) while keeping the stale index+t2g. (menu._build_kb_ref passes --overwrite; build-ref does not.) Not run against real kb (forbidden); inferred from kb source + captured cmd.
proposed_fix: Pass --overwrite, or refuse a non-empty --output without --force; assert index mtime >= combined.fa after kb ref.

evidence: repro_C/build_ref_no_overwrite_probe.py (2nd half), release 116 then 117 with one cache: downloads = [release-116 cdna.all.fa.gz, release-116 GTF, release-117 GTF]. Ensembl cDNA filename (Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.cdna.all.fa.gz) has no release number, so the cache hit reuses release-116 cDNA while the log says 'Using Ensembl release 117' and the GTF is 117. Release is always 'current' (pub/VERSION), silent fallback to hardcoded 116 on any error, no --ensembl-release option -> host reference not reproducible and cache can mix releases. Manifest release (parsed from retrieval.json source_url) stays correct only if the receipt is present.
proposed_fix: Cache under cache/<key>/release-<N>/; add --ensembl-release (pin) and record it in the manifest; fail instead of silent fallback to 116.

evidence: Fake kb + real snakemake 9.23.1 on one rule: first run OK; rm log/kb.done and rerun -> `mv out/counts_unfiltered/ out/kb-python/` fails (kb-python/counts_unfiltered exists non-empty) and job fails AFTER `mv out/*.*` moved config.yaml into kb-python/ (not moved back): run dir left without config.yaml (which rerun-multimap/hostresponse/rerun-programs require). Triggers: --resume after an interruption between the mv's, or deleting kb.done. Also `mv out/*.*` sweeps any dotted file in the sample dir.
proposed_fix: rm -rf kb-python/counts_unfiltered (or rsync) before mv; use a trap to restore config.yaml; don't glob *.*.

evidence: `--resume` with `--cores 12` against a run made with default cores -> `ERROR Cannot resume: run fingerprint does not match this invocation.` (cores is in options and hashed). Message names only --strand as a possible cause. Resubmitting a SLURM job with a different allocation cannot resume.
proposed_fix: Exclude cores/threads from the fingerprint; list the differing option names in the error.

evidence: Only existing regular files of sample1/sample2/index/transcripts/gtf/fasta/f1/whitelist/called_cells_file/host_index/positive_control_receipt are hashed. host_index is a STAR directory (is_file false -> not hashed); host_h5ad, cell_types, host_fasta, viral_fasta are only path strings; for -acc runs args.fasta/gtf are None when the manifest is built, so fetched sequence bytes are not in run_fingerprint (accession string only; unversioned accession = latest at fetch time, cached forever). --resume can therefore reuse counts after those inputs change.
proposed_fix: Hash directory contents (sorted file hashes) and the extra file inputs; record fetched FASTA/GTF sha256 and accession versions into the manifest.
